blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the South Surrey and White Rock total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Pacific Douglas
Summerfield

is a detached-house subdivision name on the feed (a current listing describes a four-bedroom house "Welcome to Summerfield!" on 172 Street) — detached freehold houses, not a strata complex, and no Summerfield condo building exists to count.

The feed labels its card "Pacific Douglas," but the project's own listing text describes it as being in "South Surrey's Grandview Heights neighbourhood," and its estimated completion ("early 2028") is listing copy only.
Streets, schools and getting around Pacific Douglas

items.t: Every visible card is labelled with the board sub-area "Pacific Douglas" and a Surrey mailing address, on streets including 18 Avenue, 19th Avenue, 172 Street, 172a Street, 1 Avenue, 171a Street and 4 Avenue — the City of Surrey's Douglas neighbourhood at the south end of South Surrey, between the two border crossings, so City of Surrey rules govern, not the City of White Rock's.

City plan area: the Douglas plan "encompass[es] an area of approximately 61 hectares (150 acres), generally located east of Hwy 99, west of Hwy 15 and north of the United States," bordered by the Agricultural Land Reserve and the Glades Garden Park to the north; the planning process concluded in 1999, and Douglas's land use designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan update. The board sub-area's feed reaches addresses north of the old NCP pocket (18/19 Avenues, 4 Avenue), so the NCP area and the board sub-area are different geographies; the street-level board boundary is not verified — FVREB publishes none.
Where condo stock concentrates: it barely does, in apartment form. SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report.

Border crossings and health care: the neighbourhood sits between the Peace Arch crossing (Highway 99, west edge) and the Pacific crossing (Highway 15 / 176 Street, east edge), per the City of Surrey; crossing hours, wait times and NEXUS specifics are not verified — no CBSA or Province page was opened. Peace Arch Hospital, 15521 Russell Avenue, White Rock, is a Fraser Health community hospital providing emergency, surgery and maternity care, open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Pacific Douglas

items.t: Surrey suites, coach houses and short-term rentals (non-ALR ground): one secondary suite per single-family, semi-detached or duplex unit, capped at 40% of the principal unit's habitable area, not within a coach house or garden suite; coach houses and garden suites 35–75 m², rising to 120 m² for lots zoned RA, R2, R2-O and R3 where the existing house or duplex is below maximum FAR. Short-term rentals: under 90 consecutive days per patron, only the owner may host from their primary residence, tenants cannot run one, and a business licence at $358 per year is required.

ALR frame for the north edge: the plan area is bordered by the Agricultural Land Reserve to the north. On ALR parcels the ALC housing frame is one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha), and subdivision — including depositing a strata plan — requires Agricultural Land Commission permission outside limited exceptions. Which specific parcels are in the ALR: check parcel by parcel on ALC mapping.

Pad rents (MHPTA) — wherever a park is discussed for this ground: manufactured-home pad rent increases are capped at 2.3% plus the proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus the proportional amount for 2027. No park in-area is named in; the cap is stated so a park unit surfaced under this label is not mistaken for strata stock.

blocks.text: Good to know about Pacific Douglas

items.t: The 1999 plan still quoted in listings no longer governs. The Douglas NCP's designations were superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update — yet a cluster of five feed listings at 148–192 172 Street quotes the NCP "Commercial/Residential" designation and an OCP "Urban" designation for the corner assembly (listing copy only; the current designation for those parcels is not verified). Read development value off the in-force OCP and Bylaw 12000 zone for the parcel, not the listing text.

The board sub-area is bigger than the City neighbourhood. The City's Douglas plan area is about 61 hectares east of Highway 99, west of Highway 15 and north of the border — but the board feed under "Pacific Douglas" reaches 18/19 Avenue and 4 Avenue addresses well north of that pocket (Berkeley Village at 16433 19 Avenue among them, with listing sources split between Pacific Douglas and Grandview filings). A "Pacific Douglas" label is a board filing, not a City boundary.

Sewer coverage here has a dated, partial official record. A 2007 City corporate report on the Douglas NCP states a City sanitary sewer system services about half the lands within the Douglas neighbourhood, primarily the more developed southwest area, flowing to the Douglas sanitary pump station. That statement is from 2007; current parcel-level servicing (City water/sewer vs well/septic) is not verified — a material check on the area's older streets.

The five-lot 172 Street cluster is one negotiation, not five listings. The feed cards at 148, 158, 172, 186 and 192 172 Street are each marketed as part of an assembly whose neighbours are also for sale — diligence and pricing should run on the combined parcel set and its current OCP/zoning position, not on any single lot's asking figure (listing prices are feed data and are not frozen here).
No official source verifies a border wait-time claim.

blocks.text: Pacific Douglas Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Pacific Douglas is the board name for the City of Surrey neighbourhood the City calls Douglas, and the City plan area is only about 61 hectares (150 acres) east of Highway 99, west of Highway 15 and north of the United States border.
The plan area's north edge is Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) land and The Glades Garden Park, which is why the streets just north of the pocket change from strata complexes to farm parcels.

blocks.text: Pacific Douglas Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: No completed apartment-condo building is verified inside Pacific Douglas, so the purchasable strata stock on this page is townhome and ground-level rancher complexes, not towers.
The Greens at Douglas, 350 174 Street, is an 83-unit 55+ rancher and townhome complex recorded as built in 2012, with age restrictions and pets allowed with restrictions in its building record.

blocks.text: Pacific Douglas Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: A 55+ bylaw is the only age bylaw a strata here may enforce: the Province states a strata may restrict residency to people age 55 or older, with exemptions for legacy residents, live-in caregivers, and younger spouses or partners — the frame for The Greens at Douglas, to be confirmed on that strata's Form B Information Certificate.

Long-term rental-restriction bylaws are void in every strata on this page, because the Province removed strata rental restrictions effective November 24, 2022; pet bylaws remain enforceable and differ by complex.

blocks.text: Pacific Douglas Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: (source report is dated 2007)

A large ALR exclusion application touches the north edge of this page's ground: application No. 7924-0241-00 covers addresses including 17081 and 17065 4 Avenue and 16900 4 Avenue, zoned CPG and A-1, and seeks to exclude about 19.8 hectares for residential purposes — see the development section.

blocks.text: Pacific Douglas Condos and Townhomes: development and new projects

items.t: Harlowe — 16485 18 Avenue, by Genaris Properties: 86 homes in total, 61 condominiums and 25 townhomes in and around a six-storey wood-frame building; status: under construction (as of November 3, 2026).

ALR exclusion application No. 7924-0241-00 — 17081 and 17065 4 Avenue and related parcels north of the Douglas pocket: exclusion of about 19.8 hectares from the Agricultural Land Reserve for residential purposes, with about 40.34 hectares of park area in the plan; status: planning report dated March 10, 2025 recommending a public hearing and referral to the Agricultural Land Commission (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Pacific Douglas Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: Driving access is the two border highways themselves: Highway 99 at the west edge and Highway 15 (176 Street) at the east edge of the plan area.

blocks.text: Pacific Douglas Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check ALR status parcel by parcel at the north edge in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR maps, because the plan area is bordered by the reserve and ALR status changes what may be built, subdivided or stratified on a parcel.

For a rancher strata in the older pocket, confirm current water and sewer servicing for the specific lot: the only servicing statement found is the City's 2007 report that about half the Douglas lands were on the City sanitary system, and that page does not tell a buyer what an individual complex is connected to today.

For The Greens at Douglas, read the registered age bylaw and the exemptions in the strata package: the provincial page explains who a 55+ bylaw may and may not exclude, but it does not reproduce this strata's own bylaw text.

Flood protection work is active on the nearby Nicomekl River system: a provincial release describes dike rehabilitation and raising protecting buildings, agricultural land and parts of 48 Avenue and 184 Street, scheduled for completion in summer 2027 — check the specific complex against the City's flood layers before relying on that work.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Pacific Douglas?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 27 condos and townhomes listed in Pacific Douglas. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Pacific Douglas a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes in Pacific Douglas had a sales ratio of not published for the month. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Pacific Douglas from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 11 condos and townhomes sold in Pacific Douglas over those 5 months, out of 456 in all of South Surrey and White Rock.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: How did Pacific Douglas sell in September 2026?
faq.a: No sub-area median is published, and the community medians (detached $1,628,000; attached $700,000) are not Pacific Douglas figures. SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report.

faq.q: Which plan guides land use in Douglas now?
faq.a: The Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026) — the City states the Douglas plan's land use designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update, with zoning under Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000.

faq.q: Can I rent out a townhome at Douglas Point or Berkeley Village long-term?
faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC.

faq.q: Which elementary school is in the neighbourhood?
faq.a: Catchment assignment for a specific home address is not verified, so check the exact address with the district before relying on it.

faq.q: Does a Douglas Green Living purchase work like a resale?
faq.a: No. While it is a presale it is a developer contract: REDMA s. 21 gives a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing and acknowledging the disclosure statement, deposits are held in trust under s. 18, and 5% GST applies to the new construction (subject to the rebates). Its completion timing is not confirmed.

faq.q: A listing quotes a Douglas NCP designation — can I rely on it for development potential?
faq.a: No. The 1999 Douglas NCP designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026); check the in-force OCP designation and the Bylaw No. 12000 zone for the specific PID.

faq.q: How big can a secondary suite be in Surrey?
faq.a: One suite per single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling, capped at 40% of the principal dwelling unit's habitable area under Zoning By-law No. 12000.

faq.q: Is Harlowe a townhouse I can buy as completed stock?
faq.a: No — Harlowe (16485 18 Ave, Genaris) is a presale of 86 homes (25 townhouses + 61 condos) with completion stated as "early 2028" by the developer, filed under Pacific Douglas by the feed and placed in Grandview Heights by its own copy — both bases carried, neither settled. It is counted in presales only, carries GST as new construction, and sits under REDMA's 7-day rescission and s. 18 trust rules.

faq.q: Can I buy an apartment condo in Pacific Douglas?
faq.a: No completed one is verified in the sub-area. The strata stock that trades here is townhome and rancher complexes — Douglas Point at 17516 4 Avenue, Berkeley Village at 16433 19 Avenue and the 55+ Greens at Douglas at 350 174 Street — plus presale product still under construction. A listing that calls a Pacific Douglas unit an apartment condo should be checked against its strata plan and civic address before it is treated as apartment stock.

faq.q: Is Douglas Point a seniors complex like The Greens at Douglas?
faq.a: No, and the two are easy to confuse because both are gated rancher-style stratas minutes apart. Under provincial law only a 55-or-older bylaw is enforceable at all, and the registered bylaw on the Form B — not a listing summary — is what governs who may live in either complex.

faq.q: Which elementary school is inside the neighbourhood?
faq.a: Douglas Elementary, at 17325 2 Avenue, is the Kindergarten to Grade 7 school physically inside this ground, listed in the British Columbia Ministry school list for School District 36 (Surrey).

faq.q: A project at 18 Avenue is labelled Pacific Douglas but its own copy says Grandview Heights — which is it?
faq.a: Unsettled, and the label should not be relied on. That project is Harlowe at 16485 18 Avenue, covered in the development section below; the board feed places it under Pacific Douglas while the project's own description places it in Grandview Heights. Confirm the sub-area from the civic address and the disclosure statement, and value the unit on its own strata documents rather than on either neighbourhood label.

faq.q: What did townhomes in Pacific Douglas sell for?
faq.a: 34 townhomes sold in Pacific Douglas between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $825,000.

faq.q: How long do townhomes take to sell in Pacific Douglas?
faq.a: The median was 19 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.2% of the last list price (0% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
